root_cause.text: The ADFS filesystem driver does not validate that the zone count (nzones) in the on-disk boot block is non-zero before using it in memory allocation and layout operations, allowing a crafted image with nzones==0 to trigger a zero-size kmalloc_array allocation and an out-of-bounds write via dm[-1] in adfs_map_layout().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if ((dr->nzones | dr->nzones_high << 8) == 0) return -EILSEQ;` in adfs_validate_bblk(). The commit message explicitly states: "When nzones is 0, adfs_read_map() passes it to kmalloc_array(0, ...) which returns ZERO_SIZE_PTR, and adfs_map_layout() then writes to dm[-1], causing an out-of-bounds write before the allocated buffer." The CVE description confirms this as the vulnerability.
